title: Documentation with KDoc
learning_outcomes: Explain the central rule or purpose of documentation with kdoc using at least one correct term from the lesson.
Interpret or adapt a small Kotlin example that demonstrates documentation with kdoc.
Identify one relevant edge case, debugging step, or version/platform constraint.

content.intro: In this lesson, you will learn **Documentation with KDoc** as part of **Testing, Debugging, Documentation, and Quality**. Reliable Kotlin code is supported by repeatable tests, meaningful assertions, debuggable failure reports, documentation, and review—not by coverage alone. Use the subtopics—Documenting Public Declarations, Parameters, Returns, and Exceptions, Generating and Maintaining API Documentation—as a checklist: predict what the example will do, then verify it in a project configured for the target platform.
content.why_it_matters: Professional applications need repeatable tests, clear APIs, dependable dependencies, security checks, and observable failures. Apply this concept in small steps before integrating it into a larger project.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: Reliable Kotlin code is supported by repeatable tests, meaningful assertions, debuggable failure reports, documentation, and review—not by coverage alone.

content_blocks.title: How to reason about it
content_blocks.text: Start with documenting public declarations. Then compare it with parameters, returns, and exceptions. Identify the input, state, dependency, or branch that determines the result. The snippet is a static reference for CodeLeaf and is not executed in the lesson page.

items.title: Documenting Public Declarations
items.text: Documenting Public Declarations is one part of documentation with kdoc. Connect its definition to the example, identify the input/state it changes, and verify the expected behavior with a small test case.

items.title: Parameters, Returns, and Exceptions
items.text: Parameters, Returns, and Exceptions describes how behavior is declared, passed, or composed. Make inputs and return types clear, keep side effects visible, and use a small call-site example to judge readability.

items.title: Generating and Maintaining API Documentation
items.text: Generating and Maintaining API Documentation crosses a system boundary. Model success and failure, validate external data, apply timeout/retry rules deliberately, and keep credentials and database access out of presentation code.

content_blocks.reset_steps: Restore the documented starting values, rerun the smallest test, and compare the result with the expected output. If behavior differs, check the compiler/plugin/runtime versions and the active target before changing more than one thing.

content_blocks.title: Common mistake to avoid
content_blocks.text: Documentation with KDoc removes the need to test boundary conditions or verify the chosen runtime/library version.

content_blocks.title: Troubleshooting and reset
content_blocks.text: If the example fails, first confirm which runtime/project type the snippet requires. Read the first useful compiler or runtime message, check imports and declared dependencies, reduce the example to a minimal case, and rerun. For target-specific code, use the target toolchain rather than assuming a console or browser runner can execute it.
